methods.sourceMethod: The midpoint and mirror-response strategy appears in both references. The solution explicitly verifies both kinds of distance restrictions and proves that play terminates.

annotationRationale: The winning construction uses central symmetry, absolute values for distances on the number line, and inequalities to verify legality and finite play. The plane distance-formula node is unnecessary. The supplied alternative guessing argument is not a proof and does not support a second method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is a reasonable classification for this finite strategy game. No repair is proposed.

review.questionCheck: Choosing n/2 and maintaining reflection symmetry gives Bela a legal reply to every Jenn move. Pairwise separation forces finite play, so Bela always wins, choice A. The shared AMC 12 statement and key agree; no figure is supplied or needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The references supply the same valid mirror strategy. Random Math's alternative guessing argument is not a proof and does not warrant another method.
review.annotationCheck: Central symmetry is appropriately assessed. Absolute value and inequality properties are genuine supports. Replacing the existing plane-distance node with cnm_007 correctly reflects the one-dimensional argument.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is a reasonable classification for this finite strategy game. No repair is proposed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Reflection preserves distance to the previously symmetric chosen set. The new pair is separated by 2|x-n/2|>2, so the reply also avoids Jenn's current move. For k selected points, summing gaps gives k-1<n and hence k<=n. Thus termination and Bela's guaranteed win both follow.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both third-party references support the midpoint strategy. The candidate independently supplies the missing current-move distance check and finite-play proof. source-informed-original is accurate; no official MAA derivation is asserted.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move is motivated by identical halves. The symmetry induction, two separate legality checks, endpoint containment, and termination argument are all explicit and accessible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_248 matches midpoint symmetry, cnm_007 supports absolute-value distances, and cnm_h018 supports the strict separation and finite bound. cnm_h173 would be inappropriate and is correctly excluded.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three native-topic links fit the used symmetry, magnitude, and inequality components. The winning-strategy synthesis goes beyond their individual mastery criteria.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-CO.A.3 offers symmetry overlap, not coverage of this game proof. 7.NS.A.1c partially supports absolute-difference distance, with rational rather than arbitrary-real scope. 6.NS.C.7 and 7c support magnitude; 7d's order-versus-magnitude distinction is not exercised. No US link is supplied for cnm_h018.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate IDs are supported. They describe the ingredients without pretending that a national standard directly covers the mirror strategy or finite-packing argument.
